key_insight: DiffSequence-Q uses quantum auxiliary supervision during training to guide protein diffusion design toward secondary structure requirements and solubility targets, while generation remains entirely classical.
engineering_relevance: The hybrid approach allows quantum models to influence protein design without requiring quantum computation during sequence generation.
method: Condition multinomial diffusion on per-residue secondary structure and a continuous solubility target.
Jointly train a shared Transformer with diffusion loss and an auxiliary solubility prediction loss from a QNN or QKAN.
Generate protein sequences through classical reverse diffusion.
evidence_signal: On CATH, DiffSequence-Q led four evaluated models in complete-generation secondary structure recovery; the best QNN and QKAN configurations scored 14.0% and 22.7% above the MLP baseline in mean predicted solubility, and selected proteins showed antifungal or enzymatic activity experimentally.
watch_item: Solubility improvements were assessed by a separate prediction model; the abstract does not establish measured solubility gains or practical quantum advantage.
paper_title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
